examples.en: My grandfather was diagnosed with lung cancer.
Lung cancer is easier to treat if found early.
The doctor said it was not lung cancer.

examples.ko: 폐암을 예방하려면 검진을 받는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: To prevent lung cancer, it's good to get screened.
My neighbor who suffered from lung cancer recovered.
Lung cancer can also be found in a health checkup.

explain: '폐'는 몸속 장기 이름이고 '암'은 병 이름이에요. '위암', '간암'처럼 장기 이름 뒤에 '암'을 붙여서 '폐암 환자', '폐암 검사'라고 써요.

phrases.en: The hospital treats lung cancer patients.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병에 걸린 사람을 말할 때 뒤에 '환자'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '환자' after it to refer to a person who has the disease.

phrases.en: I plan to get a lung cancer screening this year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병을 찾는 검사를 말할 때 '검사'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '검사' to talk about a test to check for the disease.

phrases.example: 담배를 많이 피우면 폐암에 걸릴 수 있어요.
phrases.en: If you smoke a lot, you can get lung cancer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병에 걸린다고 말할 때 '-에 걸리다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '-에 걸리다' to say someone catches or develops a disease.

explain_en: 폐 is the lung and 암 is cancer. Like 위암 and 간암, you attach 암 after the organ name, as in 폐암 환자 or 폐암 검사.

examples.en: These days I feel very tired all day.

examples.ko: 오래 운전한 날은 피로감을 많이 느껴요.
examples.en: On days I drive for a long time, I feel very fatigued.
After taking medicine, the fatigue eased a little.

examples.ko: 피로감 때문에 회의 내내 집중하기 힘들었어요.
examples.en: Because of the fatigue, it was hard to concentrate during the whole meeting.
With body aches and fatigue on top, I took a day off.
I'm suffering from fatigue and feel sleepy even during the day.

explain: '피로'는 몸이 지친 상태 자체이고, '피로감'은 그렇게 느끼는 기분이에요. 그래서 '피로감을 느끼다', '피로감이 쌓이다'처럼 말해요. 일상에서는 '피곤하다'를 훨씬 편하게 써요.

phrases.en: I feel tired because I worked a lot.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지친 기분이 든다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means you feel a sense of tiredness.

phrases.example: 며칠 동안 잠을 못 자서 피로감이 쌓였어요.
phrases.en: I could not sleep for a few days, so fatigue built up.
phrases.nuance_ko: 피로가 조금씩 많아질 때 '쌓이다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 쌓이다 when tiredness gradually increases.

phrases.en: I am so tired today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서는 '피로감'보다 이 말을 더 편하게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: In daily conversation, this is used more easily than 피로감.

explain_en: '피로' is the state of being worn out, and '피로감' is the feeling of it, so we say '피로감을 느끼다' or '피로감이 쌓이다'. In everyday speech, '피곤하다' is the more casual choice.

examples.ko: 장마철에 비가 계속 오면 피부병이 늘어요.
examples.en: When it keeps raining in the monsoon season, skin diseases increase.
The puppy caught a skin disease, so we went to the vet.

examples.ko: 피부병은 손으로 긁으면 더 심해질 수 있어요.
examples.en: A skin disease can get worse if you scratch it.

examples.ko: 피부병 약을 하루에 두 번 발라요.
examples.en: I apply the skin medicine twice a day.

examples.ko: 의사 선생님이 피부병 치료는 꾸준히 해야 한다고 했어요.
examples.en: The doctor said skin disease treatment must be kept up steadily.

examples.ko: 홍수 뒤에는 피부병과 감기가 돌기 쉬워요.
examples.en: After a flood, skin diseases and colds easily spread.

explain: '피부병에 걸리다'처럼 '걸리다'와 함께 써요. 가벼운 문제는 '피부 트러블'이라고 많이 말하고, '피부병'은 병원에서 치료가 필요한 느낌이 더 강해요.

phrases.en: I caught a skin disease after playing in dirty water.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병에 걸릴 때는 '에 걸리다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: To catch an illness, use '에 걸리다'.

phrases.en: After I applied the medicine, the skin disease got better.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병이 좋아져서 없어질 때 '낫다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 낫다 when an illness gets better and goes away.

phrases.en: I am worried about skin problems these days.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가벼운 피부 문제를 말할 때 쓰고, 피부병보다 덜 심한 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for mild skin problems; it sounds less serious than 피부병.

explain_en: It pairs with '걸리다', as in '피부병에 걸리다'. For minor problems people often say '피부 트러블', while '피부병' sounds more like something that needs medical treatment.

examples.en: A temporary building was put up next to the construction site.

examples.ko: 시장 한쪽에 가건물을 세워서 장사를 했어요.
examples.en: They set up a makeshift building at the edge of the market and sold goods.

examples.ko: 가건물은 튼튼하지 않아서 태풍이 오면 위험해요.
examples.en: Makeshift buildings aren't sturdy, so they're dangerous in a typhoon.

examples.ko: 학교를 고치는 동안 가건물에서 수업을 했어요.
examples.en: We had classes in a temporary building while the school was being repaired.

examples.ko: 행사장 앞에 있던 가건물도 곧 없어질 거예요.
examples.en: The temporary building in front of the event site will also be gone soon.
I was surprised that the temporary office was warmer than I expected.

explain: 오래 쓰려고 튼튼하게 지은 게 아니라 임시로 지은 건물이에요. 공사장 사무실, 임시 매장, 행사장 건물에 많이 쓰고, 뉴스에서는 '불법 가건물'처럼 나오기도 해요. '임시 건물'이라고 풀어서도 말해요.

phrases.example: 행사 때문에 공원에 임시 건물을 세웠어요.
phrases.en: They put up a temporary building in the park for the event.
phrases.nuance_ko: '가건물'을 풀어서 말한 쉬운 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy way to say '가건물' in plain words.

phrases.en: They are building a makeshift building next to the park.
phrases.nuance_ko: '짓다'와 함께 쓰는 가장 기본적인 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic pairing, with the verb '짓다'.

phrases.en: The city removed the illegal makeshift buildings.
phrases.nuance_ko: 허가 없이 지은 건물을 말하고 뉴스에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to buildings put up without permission and is common in the news.

explain_en: It is a building put up temporarily, not built sturdily for long use. It is used for construction-site offices, temporary shops and event buildings, and in the news it appears as '불법 가건물' (illegal temporary building). People also say it more plainly as '임시 건물'.

examples.en: Passengers watched the sea from the deck.
Waves splashed up onto the deck.
The sailors scrubbed the deck clean.
If you go out onto the deck, the wind blows hard.

examples.ko: 크루즈 갑판은 저녁이 되면 사람이 많아요.
examples.en: The cruise ship's deck gets crowded in the evening.

examples.ko: 폭풍이 오기 전에 갑판의 짐을 묶었어요.
examples.en: Before the storm, they tied down the cargo on the deck.

explain: 배 위쪽에 바깥으로 드러난 넓은 바닥이라서 '갑판에 올라가다/나가다'처럼 말해요. 배 안의 방은 '선실'이라고 해서 갑판과 구별해요. 배가 크면 '갑판'이 여러 층일 수 있어요.

phrases.en: I went out on the deck to get some fresh air.
phrases.nuance_ko: 배 안에서 바깥으로 나갈 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when going from inside the ship to the outside.

phrases.en: There are many people on the deck.
phrases.nuance_ko: 갑판의 윗면에 있는 것을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to say something is on top of the deck.

phrases.en: I watched the sunrise from the deck.
phrases.nuance_ko: 갑판이 행동이 일어나는 장소일 때 조사 '에서'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use the particle 에서 when the deck is where an action happens.

explain_en: It is the wide, open-air floor on top of a ship, so people say '갑판에 올라가다/나가다'. A room inside the ship is a '선실', which is different from the deck. A large ship can have several decks.

examples.ko: 이 마을 근처에 오래된 광산이 있어요.
examples.en: There is an old mine near this village.

examples.ko: 광산에서 일하는 사람들은 힘든 일을 해요.
examples.en: People who work in mines do hard work.
After the mine closed, people left.
That mine was famous for coal.
I was shocked to see the news about the mine accident.
The road to the mine is blocked.

explain: '탄광'은 석탄을 캐는 광산이고, 금광·은광처럼 캐는 것에 따라 이름이 달라져요. 지금은 문을 닫은 광산을 박물관이나 관광지로 쓰는 곳도 많아요.

phrases.en: There used to be a gold mine on this mountain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 금을 캐는 광산이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A mine where gold is dug.

phrases.en: My grandfather worked in a coal mine when he was young.
phrases.nuance_ko: 석탄을 캐는 광산이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A mine where coal is dug.

phrases.en: The mining town has now become a tourist spot.
phrases.nuance_ko: 광산 때문에 생긴 마을을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A town that grew up around a mine.

explain_en: A '탄광' is a coal mine, and the name changes with what is dug, such as '금광' (gold mine) and '은광' (silver mine). Many closed mines are now used as museums or tourist spots.

examples.en: There are many bridges over the Han River.
The new bridge is scheduled to be completed next year.
The road is jammed because of the bridge construction.

examples.ko: 오래된 교량은 안전 점검을 받아야 해요.
examples.en: Old bridges need safety inspections.
Once you cross this bridge, you are right in the city.

examples.ko: 밤이 되면 교량들은 조명이 켜져서 예뻐요.
examples.en: At night the bridges are lit up and look pretty.

explain: 일상에서는 '다리'가 훨씬 흔해요. '교량'은 공사, 뉴스, 안내문에서 쓰는 격식 있는 말이에요. 사람이나 일이 둘 사이를 이어 줄 때 '교량 역할'이라고 비유해서도 써요.

phrases.example: 그 통역사가 두 회사의 교량 역할을 해요.
phrases.en: serve as a bridge between two sides
phrases.nuance_ko: 서로 다른 둘을 이어 주는 사람이나 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a person or thing that connects two different sides.

explain_en: In daily life '다리' is far more common. '교량' is the formal word used in construction, news, and notices. It is also used figuratively, as in '교량 역할', for someone or something that connects two sides.

examples.ko: 요즘은 교통난 때문에 출근이 정말 힘들어요.
examples.en: These days commuting is really hard because of the traffic problems.
Traffic problems in big cities get worse every year.

examples.ko: 교통난을 줄이려고 버스 전용 차로를 늘렸어요.
examples.en: They added bus-only lanes to reduce traffic congestion.
Highway traffic is especially bad in the vacation season.

examples.ko: 교통난에 시달리다 보니 지하철을 타기로 했어요.
examples.en: After suffering from the traffic, I decided to take the subway.

examples.ko: 교통난만 아니면 회사 근처에 살 필요가 없을 텐데요.
examples.en: If it weren't for the traffic, I wouldn't need to live near work.

explain: 차가 막히는 것뿐 아니라 도로, 주차, 대중교통이 모자라서 생기는 도시의 교통 문제 전체를 말해요. 일상에서 막히는 길은 '교통 체증'이나 '차가 막히다'라고 해요. '주택난', '취업난'처럼 '-난'이 붙은 말과 같이 알아 두세요.

phrases.example: 새 지하철이 교통난을 줄여 줄 거예요.
phrases.en: The new subway will reduce traffic problems.
phrases.nuance_ko: 도시의 교통 문제가 나아지게 한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means making a city's traffic problems better.

phrases.en: Citizens suffer traffic trouble every morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람들이 불편을 직접 경험한다는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Gives the feeling that people experience the trouble directly.

phrases.en: Traffic jams are bad at rush hour.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서 길이 막히는 것을 말할 때 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used more often in daily life for roads being jammed.

explain_en: It covers not only jammed roads but the city's whole transport problem from shortages of roads, parking and public transit. In daily talk, a jammed road is '교통 체증' or '차가 막히다'. It is handy to learn it with other '-난' words like '주택난' and '취업난'.

examples.en: The road winds on and on.
We climbed up the winding mountain path.
The river winds through the fields.
My hair is wavy, so I straighten it every day.
I got lost in the winding alleys.
The snake slithered away in curves.

explain: 길, 강, 머리카락처럼 길쭉한 것이 이리저리 굽은 모양이에요. '구불구불하다'로도 쓰고, 길이 꼬불꼬불한 건 '꼬불꼬불'이 더 작고 촘촘한 느낌이에요. 곧은 모양은 '쭉' 또는 '똑바로'라고 해요.

phrases.en: I walked slowly along the winding road.
phrases.nuance_ko: '구불구불' 뒤에 '한'을 붙이면 명사를 꾸밀 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 한 lets it describe a noun.

phrases.en: The river winds its way through the village.
phrases.nuance_ko: 강물처럼 길게 이어지는 것에 동사와 함께 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used with verbs for long things like a flowing river.

phrases.en: My hair is wavy.
phrases.nuance_ko: '하다'를 붙여 형용사처럼 쓰면 머리카락 모양도 말할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: With 하다 it works like an adjective, even for wavy hair.

explain_en: It describes long things like roads, rivers and hair bending this way and that. It also works as '구불구불하다'. '꼬불꼬불' feels smaller and tighter, while straight shapes are '쭉' or '똑바로'.

examples.en: We're in the mountains, so there is no cell tower nearby.

examples.ko: 기지국이 고장 나서 전화가 안 터져요.
examples.en: The base station broke down, so phone calls won't connect.
A new cell tower was built and the internet got faster.
The carrier decided to build more base stations.

examples.ko: 기지국 근처에 살면 전파가 강하게 잡혀요.
examples.en: If you live near a cell tower, the signal is strong.

examples.ko: 건물 옥상에 기지국 안테나가 설치되어 있어요.
examples.en: A base station antenna is installed on the rooftop.

explain: 휴대폰 신호 이야기에서 '기지국'은 '전파가 터지다', '통신망'과 함께 나와요. 안테나 하나가 아니라 신호를 받아 전달하는 시설 전체를 가리켜서 '안테나'와는 구별해서 써요.

phrases.en: The base station signal is weak in this room.
phrases.nuance_ko: 휴대폰이 받는 전파 상태를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when talking about the phone signal you receive.

phrases.en: The company built a new base station in the village.
phrases.nuance_ko: 통신 시설을 새로 만드는 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a new communication facility is built.

phrases.example: 가까운 기지국에 연결돼서 전화가 잘 터져요.
phrases.en: My phone connects to a nearby base station, so calls go through well.
phrases.nuance_ko: 휴대폰이 어느 기지국에 연결되는지 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when describing which base station a phone connects to.

explain_en: In talk about phone signals, '기지국' goes with '전파가 터지다' (the signal comes through) and '통신망' (network). It means the whole facility that receives and relays signals, not just one antenna, so it is kept distinct from '안테나'.

examples.ko: 집 앞에 기찻길이 있어서 기차 소리가 들려요.
examples.en: There is a railroad in front of my house, so I can hear the trains.
When I was little, I walked along the railroad.
The railroad is dangerous, so you must not cross it.
A train passes slowly over the tracks.
The old railroad has been turned into a walking path.
I stopped for a moment at the railroad crossing.

explain: '철길'과 같은 뜻으로 쓰는 말이에요. '철도'는 열차 교통 전체를 말할 때가 많고, '기찻길'은 열차가 다니는 길 그 자체를 말할 때 써요.

phrases.en: There is a small village beside the railroad.
phrases.nuance_ko: '기찻길'과 같은 뜻으로 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Interchangeable with 기찻길.

phrases.example: 기찻길 옆에 살아서 밤에도 소리가 들려요.
phrases.en: I live next to the railroad, so I hear the trains even at night.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기찻길 근처의 장소를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for places near the tracks.

phrases.en: Be careful when you cross the railroad tracks.
phrases.nuance_ko: 안전 이야기에서 자주 나오는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A phrase often heard in safety talk.

explain_en: It means the same as '철길'. '철도' often refers to the whole railway system, while '기찻길' refers to the path the train runs on.

examples.en: The area near the landfill smells terrible.

examples.ko: 이 공항은 바다를 메운 매립지에 지었어요.
examples.en: This airport was built on land reclaimed from the sea.

examples.ko: 매립지가 꽉 차서 새 장소를 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: The landfill is full, so they are looking for a new site.
Families ride bikes in the landfill park.
The news is covering the landfill problem.

examples.ko: 쓰레기를 줄이면 매립지로 가는 양이 줄어요.
examples.en: If we reduce trash, the amount going to landfills decreases.

explain: '쓰레기 매립지'로 가장 많이 듣고, 바다를 메워 만든 땅도 매립지라고 해요. 둘 다 흙이나 쓰레기로 메운 곳이라는 점이 같아요. 뉴스에서 환경 문제를 이야기할 때 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: They bury the trash in a landfill.
phrases.nuance_ko: 쓰레기 처리 방법을 말할 때 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing when talking about how trash is disposed of.

phrases.en: The landfill is almost full.
phrases.nuance_ko: 환경 문제를 이야기할 때 뉴스에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often heard in the news about environmental problems.

phrases.en: They built the airport on reclaimed land by the sea.
phrases.nuance_ko: 메워서 만든 땅 위에 건물을 세운다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means building on land that was filled in.

explain_en: You hear it most in 쓰레기 매립지 (waste landfill), and land made by filling in the sea is also 매립지. Both are places filled in with soil or trash. It is common in environmental news.

examples.en: It rained a lot and the waterway got blocked.
The farmer made a water channel to the rice field.

examples.ko: 배는 좁은 물길을 따라 천천히 갔어요.
examples.en: The boat went slowly along the narrow waterway.
The sound of the stream coming from the mountain is refreshing.
The course of the water changed after the typhoon.
In the old days they carried goods by water route.

explain: '강'이나 '바다'처럼 이름이 있는 큰 물이 아니라, 물이 흘러가는 길 자체를 말해요. '물길을 내다', '물길이 막히다'처럼 써요. 땅 위의 길은 '길', 바다 위 길은 '뱃길'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: The villagers made a water channel to the field.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물이 흐르도록 길을 만들 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when making a path for water to flow.

phrases.en: The waterway was blocked by trash.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물이 흐르지 못할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when water cannot flow.

phrases.en: I walked slowly along the waterway.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물이 흐르는 길을 따라 움직일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for moving along a water route.

explain_en: It is the path water flows along, not a named river or sea. Common uses are 물길을 내다 and 물길이 막히다. A road on land is a 길, and a route over the sea is a 뱃길.

examples.en: When you board the bus, please tap your transit card.
I checked my ticket before boarding the train.
No one boards through the back door.
Passengers line up and board in order.
I got on at Seoul Station.

examples.ko: 승차할 때 아이 손을 꼭 잡으세요.
examples.en: Hold your child's hand tightly when boarding.

explain: 반대말은 '하차하다'예요. 안내 방송이나 표지판에서 많이 보이고, 말할 때는 '타다'가 훨씬 자연스러워요. '승차'는 탈것에 타는 일, 즉 버스·기차·택시 등에 써요.

phrases.en: You have to buy a ticket first.
phrases.nuance_ko: 버스나 기차를 탈 때 필요한 표를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The ticket you need to ride a bus or train.

phrases.en: Please get off at the next station.
phrases.nuance_ko: '승차하다'의 반대말로, 안내 방송에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of 승차하다; often heard in announcements.

phrases.en: I go to school by bus.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말할 때는 '승차하다'보다 '타다'가 훨씬 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: In speech, 타다 is much more natural than 승차하다.

explain_en: The opposite is '하차하다' (get off). You see it on announcements and signs; in speech '타다' is far more natural. It is for vehicles like buses, trains and taxis.
